_meta.note: Usage context of every UI text key (SPEC-v2 P14.8.1 step 2): where (button|label|tooltip|title|toast|error|empty|dialog|menu|placeholder|status), max (characters the layout can show; null = free), params (meaning of each {param}), notes. Translators must respect max.

common.remove.notes: Removes an item from a list (e.g. a waiting upload); nothing is deleted on the server.

common.download.notes: Opens the menu of export files of a lecture.

common.zh_edit_note.notes: Small line under an editor of Chinese lecture content (a glossary rendering, a Chinese lecture title) while Chinese content is shown in Traditional characters (P14.6): the editor shows the stored Simplified text; what is typed is saved as it is and only converted for display.

common.choose_files.notes: Button inside a drop zone; opens the file picker.

common.load_failed.notes: Bold heading of an error block inside a card, followed by the error text and a Retry button.

common.toast_close.notes: Accessible name of the x button of a toast notice.

common.link_throttled.notes: Desktop app only. Shown when a click on an external link (release page, provider sign-up page …) did nothing because the app opens at most 3 links in 10 seconds; the person only has to wait a moment and click again.

common.dont_cancel.notes: Dismisses a 'cancel processing?' confirmation without cancelling anything.

common.list_sep.notes: Separator between items of an inline list (file names, stage names). Keep the spacing your language needs.

params.n: a number of bytes under 1000, formatted (0–999; plural forms)

common.size_bytes.notes: Round 9 (T28 G7): a file or download size under 1000 bytes, e.g. the size beside a small export file (the English text) in the lecture page's download menu, and sizes inside other texts. 1000 bytes and more are written by the code with the language's kB / MB / GB (1 kB = 1000 bytes). Intl's own word was English “byte” in Traditional Chinese: zh-TW and yue-Hant-HK write 位元組 (as errors.upload.media_empty does), ru байт, hi बाइट. Keep {n} and the spacing your language puts between a number and its unit (zh-CN writes 714字节 without a space).

common.markdown_rest_plain.notes: Markdown preview (the syllabus preview of the add-course wizard and the course page, and the third-party notices in Settings > About): a line in italics where the formatting stops in a very long or malformed document (past about 300 000 page elements). Above it, the document formatted; below it, the rest of the document as plain text.

common.clause_sep.notes: Separator between clauses of a compound note, or between several reasons. Keep the spacing your language needs.

params.pct: share of the lecture already transcribed, e.g. 38%

common.status.queued_checkpoint.notes: Status of a transcription stage that the power-aware policy put back in line (charger pulled, or moved to another device): it is waiting, but its checkpoint already holds this share of the lecture, and the next run continues from there instead of starting over. Shown in the stage card, the screen-reader label of the bar segment and the transcript page. Keep the word for checkpoint the same as common.pipe.k_checkpoint.

common.status.running_preparing.notes: Round 7 (T25 G1, G2): the state of a running stage that has not reported any progress yet, instead of “运行中 0%” (common.status.running_pct). Shown in the stage card, the segment's label for screen readers and the lecture page.

common.status.running_preparing_asr.notes: Round 7 (T25 G2): as common.status.running_preparing, for a transcription on this computer: in its first seconds or minutes it loads the speech model and finds where the lecture has speech, before any share is reported.

common.status.running_resuming.notes: R79 M3: a transcription on this computer run again (a retry, the restart after the app was closed) that has not reported progress yet: it continues from its checkpoint when there is one for the same device and model, else it starts over — so no promise: “may” (R79b: a checkpoint of another device, model or precision is discarded). Not used for a remote transcription or a translation.

common.action.cancel.notes: Cancels a running or queued stage.

common.action.use_colab.notes: Button on the transcription stage's card (pipeline hover card) when Colab handed the lecture back and this computer has no transcription device that could take it (waiting.remote_fallback). Same action and wording as the lecture menu item menu.lecture.use_colab (“Process on Colab instead”, 改用 Colab 处理, SPEC-v3 V14.4): the transcription starts over on Google Colab after a confirmation. No period.

common.action.rerun_text_only.notes: Button on the transcription stage's card (pipeline hover card) and lecture context menu item, offered only when the transcript is worth repairing. “Fix sentence breaks” (修复断句, textrepair-int): for a lecture transcribed before LectureFlow learned to repair degenerate Whisper output, the transcript's long runs without punctuation and its all-caps passages are repaired by statistics learned from the same lecture's normal text (full stops added, capitals restored), and the sentences are split again. It does not transcribe the audio again. The same name is the confirm button (lecture.text_repair.ok). Short; no period.

common.action.retry_model.notes: Button next to Retry on the card of a failed or cancelled summary, repair or translate stage, and lecture menu item: opens the model dialog of the retry (v3.2.x P1-b) whatever the recorded model. The ellipsis says a dialog follows.

common.class.auto.notes: Class of an AI repair: applied automatically.

common.class.absorb.notes: Class of an AI repair: minor, the translation absorbs it.

common.class.decide.notes: Class of an AI repair: the user should listen and decide.

common.review_state.none.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

common.review_state.pending.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

common.review_state.accepted.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

common.review_state.rejected.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

common.review_state.edited.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

params.model: model name, e.g. deepseek-chat

common.check.role_model.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: a model that roles use but the provider's model list no longer has.

common.check.openvino_venv.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: whether .venv-ov exists (phase 3b).

common.check.openvino_devices.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: the Intel GPU / NPU / CPU that OpenVINO detected.

common.check.npu_driver.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: whether the NPU driver works.

common.check.mlx_python.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on macOS (mac-opti M3): the MLX transcription environment (asr-mlx component) is installed and its Python runs. The check named mlx (import) shows the product name MLX.

common.check.mlx_model.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on macOS (mac-opti M3): the files of the Apple GPU's Whisper model are there.

common.check.mlx_selftest.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on Apple silicon Macs (ext-step1): the MLX model transcribes one second of silence (run by “Check again”). Like common.check.cuda.

common.check.cpu_selftest.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on computers without an NVIDIA GPU or Apple silicon (ext-step1): one second of silence transcribed on the CPU (run by “Check again”).

common.check.colab_auth.notes: Name of a diagnostics check in the cloud group (ext-step1): a stored Google Colab credential.

common.check.colab_reach.notes: Name of a diagnostics check in the cloud group (ext-step1): Google Colab answers a free read-only request.

common.check.aria2c.notes: Name of a diagnostics row. aria2c is the download engine bundled with LectureFlow; it fetches lecture recordings for the browser extension and downloads app updates. {version} is the first line of `aria2c --version` (e.g. “aria2 version 1.37.0”), {sha256} a 64-character hex hash. Recording-related wording uses “fetch” (刮削), never “download”, by the user's decision.

common.check.browser_ext.notes: Name of a diagnostics row. The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), {browser} one name, {version} the extension's version, {at} a local time “YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM”. “Register again” (重新登记) is the button next to the row.

common.check.credentials.notes: Name of a diagnostics check (#/system): how the saved API keys and the Colab authorization are encrypted at rest (cred-enc).

common.check.data_dir_location.notes: Name of a diagnostics check (#/system), shown only with a warning: the data folder is in a cloud sync folder or on a FAT/exFAT drive.

common.check.install_dir.notes: Name of a diagnostics check (#/system), shown only in the Windows desktop app installed by its installer: whether other accounts of the computer can change the folder LectureFlow's programs are installed in.

common.stream_status.ready.notes: State of the playback file (stream.mp4), inserted as {stream_status} into notes.

common.stream_status.audio_only.notes: State of the playback file (stream.mp4), inserted as {stream_status} into notes.

common.stream_status.no_space.notes: State of the playback file (stream.mp4), inserted as {stream_status} into notes.

common.stream_status.failed.notes: State of the playback file (stream.mp4), inserted as {stream_status} into notes.

params.wait: what it waits for, e.g. 'Retrying automatically in 30 seconds'
what it waits for, or the status 'Waiting'

params.summary: the lecture's status line (already translated), e.g. 'Transcription: Suspended: power-aware - waiting for the power adapter'
params.pct: share of the lecture already transcribed, e.g. 38%

common.summary.checkpoint.notes: Lecture row status line (course page, dashboard, lecture page) of a lecture whose transcription is waiting after a power interrupt: the summary followed by how much its checkpoint already holds. Same wording as common.status.queued_checkpoint after the status.

common.pipe.label.notes: Accessible name of the segmented progress bar of a lecture.

common.pipe.k_wait.notes: Row label in a stage card; the value is what the stage waits for.

common.pipe.k_note.notes: Row label in a stage card.

common.pipe.k_attempts.notes: Row label in a stage card; the value says how often it was retried.

common.pipe.k_time.notes: Row label in a stage card; the value is a duration. Round 9 (TX-04, needs-human 一·16b): it is the time of this stage's latest run only: how long that run took once it ended (“7 s”), or common.pipe.elapsed while it runs (“Running for 2 min”); the label must read well before both. A run that goes on after a cancel or a restart counts from its own start, without the time before (started_at is set again at every start). There is no total across runs; do not call it total or overall. Like common.pipe.k_waited (本次请求 / This request).

common.pipe.k_tokens.notes: Row label in a stage card; the value is the token usage.

common.pipe.k_model.notes: Row label in a stage card.

common.pipe.k_device.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card: device name · model · precision · language.

common.pipe.k_asr_time.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card; the value is how long the transcription itself took (without loading the model), with the length of the audio.

params.time: duration of the transcription, e.g. '1 min 46 s'
params.audio: length of the audio, e.g. '52 min 0 s'

common.pipe.k_speed.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card; the value is the real-time factor and how many times faster than real time the transcription ran.

params.rtf: real-time factor = transcription time ÷ audio length, e.g. '0.034'
params.speed: how many times faster than real time (1 ÷ rtf), e.g. '29'

common.pipe.rtf.notes: Keep the abbreviation RTF (real-time factor) as it is: it is the number shown in the device test results too.

common.pipe.k_load.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card; the value is how long loading the model took.

common.pipe.k_parts.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card: the run was resumed on another device (power-aware), one line per part.

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)
params.combo: model and precision, e.g. large-v3-turbo · fp16 (not translated)

common.pipe.part.notes: One part of a resumed transcription in the stage card.

common.pipe.k_checkpoint.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card while the stage waits after a power interrupt; the value says how far the saved checkpoint reaches. Same word as in common.status.queued_checkpoint.

params.at: position in the lecture the checkpoint reaches, e.g. 21:16

common.pipe.checkpoint.notes: Value of the checkpoint row in the transcription stage card: transcribed up to this point of the lecture; the next run continues from there (it does not start over).

common.pipe.load_first_compile.notes: Model load time of the first use of a model on an Intel GPU / NPU: it includes compiling the model into the cache, which happens only once.

common.pipe.k_error.notes: Heading of the error box of a failed stage.

common.pipe.k_warning.notes: Heading of the warning box of a stage that finished with a warning.

common.pipe.k_last_error.notes: Heading of the error box of a stage that failed before and is now retrying.

common.pipe.corrupt_hint.notes: Shown under the error of a stage that failed because the media file is incomplete or damaged (errors.media.corrupt): Retry runs the same file again, so the user should import a complete file instead.

common.pipe.open_settings.notes: Round 7 (T24 S3, T22 G7): a link styled as a button, in the lecture page's failure notice and in the stage card, for a failure fixed in Settings (a missing or refused API key, a provider not set up, base_url or the model name, a role without a model). Opens Settings at the section that fixes it (providers or roles).

common.pipe.tech_details.notes: Round 7 (T24 G2): the summary of a collapsed section in a stage's hover card, under the translated error or warning: opens the program's original message (often in Chinese, with the server's response), which the user rarely needs; “复制完整错误” (common.pipe.copy_error) copies it whole.

common.pipe.pct_stage.notes: Round 7 (T25 G9): beside the lecture page's stage bar, the share of the stage that runs now (the bar itself has six segments, so a lone number read as the whole lecture's progress and jumped back at each new stage). Short: a stage name and a number.

common.pipe.pct_tip.notes: Round 7 (T25 G9): hover of the percentage beside a stage bar (lecture rows show the number alone).

common.pipe.eta_soon.notes: Round 7 (T25 S2, T22 G2): a rough time left for a running stage, after “已运行 …” in its card and after the lecture page's status (“正在转写 · …”): less than a minute. Estimated from the share done so far; a rough figure, so “about”.

common.pipe.eta_m.notes: Round 7 (T25 S2): as common.pipe.eta_soon, in minutes.

common.pipe.eta_hm.notes: Round 7 (T25 S2): as common.pipe.eta_soon, an hour or more. May be written as a plural object chosen by the number of hours {h} (it is passed as n as well), for a language whose word for hours changes with the number (I64: Hindi घंटा / घंटे); every form keeps {h} and {m}.

common.pipe.eta_h.notes: R79 L3: as common.pipe.eta_hm when the time left, rounded to 5 minutes, is whole hours (no “0 minutes”).

params.model: model name (not translated)

common.pipe.model_unlisted.notes: Round 7 (T24 S3, T22 G8): under the error of a stage whose request was refused as for an unknown model (HTTP 404 or 400) when that model is not in the provider's last fetched model list; shown in full on the lecture page and in the stage card. The model may have been retired or its name mistyped (the same answer either way; R72 L5). “换模型重试…” is the button common.action.retry_model, “角色分配” the settings section settings.block.roles: quote both as those keys are translated.

params.role: role name (translated by the front end): summary, correction or translation
params.model: model name

common.lecture_error.llm.refusal.notes: Round 9 (T28 suggestion 2): errors.llm.refusal as the lecture page's banner and the stage cards of a lecture's summary, correction and translation say it. Those stages have the button “换模型重试…” (common.action.retry_model; quote it exactly as that key is translated), offered first, so only that way out is given: the same sentence as errors.llm.refusal without the part about Settings → Roles, which is for the other tasks and is still said where they fail (errors.llm.refusal). Keep the wording of errors.llm.refusal up to there.

params.role: role name (translated by the front end): summary, correction or translation
params.seconds: the time limit of one request in seconds
params.model: model name

common.lecture_error.llm.time_limit.notes: Round 9 (T28 suggestion 2): errors.llm.time_limit as the lecture page's banner and the stage cards of a lecture's summary, correction and translation say it (see common.lecture_error.llm.refusal): only the way out by “换模型重试…” (common.action.retry_model, quoted exactly as translated), whose dialog has the thinking level (“there”); the provider and the model are named in the first parentheses, as errors.llm.refusal names them. The rules of errors.llm.time_limit hold: do not assume thinking is on, do not suggest a lower output limit or fewer sentences per request.

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

common.retrying.llm.network.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.llm.network as it is said while the stage waits for its automatic retry (a countdown shows beside it, and there is no Retry button): the same sentence without “then select Retry”. Keep the wording of errors.llm.network up to that advice. The family common.retrying.{code} follows errors.{code} this way.

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)
params.seconds: the time limit of one request in seconds

common.retrying.llm.timeout.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.llm.timeout without “Select Retry later”, shown while an automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.network).

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

common.retrying.llm.idle_timeout.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.llm.idle_timeout without “Select Retry later” (the gateway advice stays), shown while an automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.network).

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

common.retrying.llm.server_error.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.llm.server_error without “Select Retry later”, shown while an automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.network).

common.retrying.prep.file_in_use.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.prep.file_in_use without “then select Retry”, shown while an automatic retry is pending: closing the program is enough, the retry comes by itself (see common.retrying.llm.network).

params.name: file name of one export file, as in errors.export.file_in_use

common.retrying.export.file_in_use.notes: Round 7 (T24 G5): errors.export.file_in_use without “then select Retry”, shown while an automatic retry is pending: closing the program is enough, the retry comes by itself (see common.retrying.llm.network).

params.role: role name (translated by the front end)

common.retrying.llm.bad_response.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.llm.bad_response as it is said while the stage waits for or runs its automatic retry (a countdown shows beside it, no Retry button): the same sentence without the advice to retry or to change the model. The scheduler retries a failed stage by itself at most twice (after 10 s, then 60 s; internal/sched scheduler.go, model.MaxAutoRetries, RetryBackoffSeconds), never an auxiliary task; after the last one errors.llm.bad_response is shown with its advice. Do not say it keeps retrying.

common.retrying.stage.output_unusable.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.stage.output_unusable without the advice, while the automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.bad_response).

common.retrying.translate.sentences_fail.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.translate.sentences_failed while the automatic retry is pending or running (see common.retrying.llm.bad_response): instead of “select Retry”, that this retry translates only these sentences again (the translate stage only sends sentences without a usable translation).

common.retrying.stage.sentences_changed.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.stage.sentences_changed without “select Retry”, while the automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.bad_response).

common.retrying.asr.worker_failed.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.asr.worker_failed while the automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.llm.bad_response): what happened and the process in parentheses, without the advice (retry, another device, diagnostics), which errors.asr.worker_failed gives if the retries fail too. Exit code 2 is never retried (errors.asr.worker_input_error).

common.retrying.asr.worker_error.notes: Round 8 (WL-09): errors.asr.worker_error while the automatic retry is pending (see common.retrying.asr.worker_failed).

common.pipe.stream_generating.notes: Hover card of the preprocessing stage, value of the line “Playback file” (stage.stream): the video had to be converted, so its playback file (the browser-playable video) is being made by a separate task after preprocessing, in parallel with transcription and the later stages (stream-parallel). common.pipe.stream_ready_transcoded.notes: Hover card of the preprocessing stage, value of the line “Playback file”: the playback file exists and was made by converting the video (not just repackaged). SPEC-v2 P8.1 asks to say “converted” on the lecture page.

common.pipe.stream_pending.notes: Hover card of the preprocessing stage, value of the line “Playback file”: a lecture prepared by an old version has no playback file yet; opening the player starts making it.

common.pipe.stream_bg_label.notes: Screen-reader text added to the preprocessing segment of the progress bar while the playback file is being made in the background (a small play mark on the segment); joined to the segment label with common.clause_sep.

common.pipe.manual_tag.notes: Small tag after the model line of a stage hover card: the model was named by hand for one retry (common.model_choice.manual), not taken from the settings.

common.pipe.max_tokens.notes: Part of the model line and of the attempt line of a stage hover card: the output limit sent with the request. Keep max_tokens untranslated.

common.pipe.k_request.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Row label; the value is the current attempt or the number of requests in flight.

common.pipe.attempt_n.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Start of the line “Attempt 2 · model · max_tokens 32,768”. An ordinal, not a count.

params.s: seconds left, counts down every second

common.pipe.retry_in.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. The request waits out a backoff before its next attempt.

common.pipe.retry_due.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. The backoff is over; the next attempt is about to be sent.

common.pipe.phase_thinking.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. A streamed request: the model is thinking (no answer text yet).

common.pipe.phase_writing.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. A streamed request: the answer text is arriving.

common.pipe.in_flight.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Stages that send many requests at once (translate, repair).

common.pipe.last_outcome.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. How the last finished attempt ended, shown when it did not succeed.

common.pipe.outcome.ok.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome of an attempt ({outcome}, {result}); lower case where the language allows.

common.pipe.outcome.truncated.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the answer reached max_tokens and was cut off.

common.pipe.outcome.truncated_thinking.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: max_tokens was used up by thinking before any answer text.

common.pipe.outcome.timeout.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: no answer within the request timeout.

common.pipe.outcome.network.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the connection failed.

common.pipe.outcome.http_error.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the provider answered with an HTTP error.

common.pipe.outcome.idle.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: a streamed request sent nothing for longer than the idle timeout.

common.pipe.outcome.refused.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the model refused to answer.

common.pipe.outcome.bad_response.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the answer could not be read.

common.pipe.outcome.canceled.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Outcome: the request was cancelled.

common.pipe.k_activity.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Row label; the value is how long ago the run last showed life (common.pipe.ago_*).

common.pipe.ago_s.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Value of common.pipe.k_activity under a minute.

common.pipe.ago_ms.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Value of common.pipe.k_activity from a minute on.

common.pipe.k_waited.notes: Stage hover card (pipeline bar) of an LLM stage (summary, repair, translate), v3.2.x P1-c: what the run's requests are doing. Row label; the value is common.pipe.waited.

nav.notify.download_retry_window.notes: Added to the notification of a failed recording fetch that a retry can fix: after that time LectureFlow forgets the sign-in for safety (errors.downloads.credentials_cleared). Round 8 (R76 L-12): it follows the error, which often already says to retry (errors.downloads.network), so it says only how long a retry works and what to do after that, without repeating “retry to continue”; en in two short sentences. The sign-in lives in memory only, so a restart of LectureFlow ends it too (errors.downloads.restarted); a fetch whose tracks are all on disk (merging or creating the lecture failed) can still be retried after that time without the extension (internal/fetch queue.go sweepCredentials, Retry).

Changed (nm-harden, 2026-10-27): this LectureFlow could not open that local connection because another program already holds it (a second LectureFlow, or some other program that took the name first). The extension therefore cannot reach this LectureFlow. Do not suggest that the extension works through the other program: earlier versions of this text did, and it is not true. The hint (errors.check.hint_browser_ext_in_use) says what to do.

errors.llm.time_limit.notes: The answer was still being written when the time limit of one request ran out; it is not retried automatically. The advice must not assume thinking is on (it may be off for the role). Do not suggest lowering the output limit: the time limit scales with it, so a lower limit only turns the timeout into a truncated answer billed again. Do not suggest sending fewer sentences per request either: a batch request that runs out of time is split automatically, and the time limit of a single-sentence request grows with the sentences-per-request setting. Round 7 (T24 B1): the text names the button “换模型重试…” (common.action.retry_model, quote it exactly as that key is translated), offered first for this error; “there” is that button's dialog, whose “临时指定” choice has the thinking level. Round 8 (C175d): the advice says where each way applies — the button for a lecture's summary, correction and translation, Settings → Roles (settings.block.roles) for the other tasks — as errors.llm.refusal and errors.llm.bad_response do.

errors.pdf.decode_budget.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF: lecture slides (shown on the course page's slide row) or a PDF syllabus (shown in the syllabus wizard after uploading). Security review: the PDF's compressed contents unpack to far more data than any real slides or syllabus (a typical sign of a file built to exhaust the computer's memory), so LectureFlow stopped instead of continuing. Not retried automatically; a damaged or exotic export can also cause it, hence the advice to export the PDF again (e.g. from PowerPoint or the original program).

errors.pdf.memory_limit.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF (lecture slides on the course page, or a PDF syllabus in the syllabus wizard). Security review: the text extraction process has a fixed memory limit so that a malicious or broken PDF cannot use up the computer's memory; this PDF needed more, so it was stopped. Not retried automatically. Same pattern as errors.pdf.decode_budget.

errors.pdf.timeout.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF (lecture slides on the course page, or a PDF syllabus in the syllabus wizard). Security review: the extraction has a time limit that grows with the file size and the number of pages (real slides take a few seconds); this PDF took longer, so the process was stopped. Not retried automatically. Same pattern as errors.pdf.decode_budget; “min” as in errors.colab.queue_timeout.

errors.export.file_in_use.notes: Error of the export step (the lecture's last step, which writes the bilingual Markdown, the two subtitle files, the English text and the citation JSON), shown on the lecture page and in the pipeline card. Windows only: another program (an editor such as Word, a viewer, a download that is still running) has this export file open, so the new export could not replace it. Nothing was changed: all the old export files are still there and still downloadable. LectureFlow tries again by itself a few times; after closing the program the user can select the stage's “Retry” button (common.action.retry). Use the same wording for that button as in common.action.retry.

errors.media.no_h264_encoder.notes: Error of the playback-file step (SPEC-v3 V7): the video needs converting but no H.264 encoder can be used, so the player opens in audio mode. Shown on the lecture page and in the player.

errors.media.encoder_failed.notes: Error of the playback-file step (SPEC-v3 V7, qsv-retry): the video had to be converted to H.264 and the video encoder itself failed (e.g. the graphics chip's hardware encoder glitched under load), also after a second try and with every other usable encoder. The file is fine and trying again may work, so the player opens in audio mode meanwhile. Shown on the lecture page and in the player after “Could not create the playback file:” (player.audio.failed). params.tried (encoder names) is not shown.

errors.media.format_rejected.notes: Error of preprocessing (the lecture's prep step) or of the playback-file step, shown on the lecture page, in the pipeline card and in the player after “Could not create the playback file:”. The lecture's stored media file turned out to be a playlist or a container outside the accepted list. Security review 2 (M3): ffmpeg follows playlists (HLS .m3u8, ffconcat scripts), which could make it read other files on the computer or connect to a network share with the user's Windows credentials, so LectureFlow refuses them. New uploads are already checked (errors.upload.media_format); this covers media stored earlier or added another way. A started lecture's media cannot be replaced, so the remedy is converting the file and uploading it again. Same meaning as errors.upload.media_format, without the file name.

errors.data_import.modified.notes: Settings → data folder → import an existing data folder (desktop app). The folder is a LectureFlow data folder, but its database holds things the app itself never writes: a table, column, view or trigger someone added or changed with a database tool, or a record id or file name in a form the app never uses. Such a database could make the app read or delete files outside the library, so the import is refused as a whole. Not an accusation: the user may simply have opened the database in a tool. "Library" is the user's collection of courses and lectures (资料库). The end as in the other errors.*: no full stop in the Chinese texts (zh-CN, zh-TW, yue), the sentence-final mark in the others (en: a period).

params.count: how many stored file paths point elsewhere (a number ≥ 1)
params.path: one of those paths as stored, e.g. C:\Users\name\Documents\notes.pdf

errors.data_import.outside_path.notes: Settings → data folder → import an existing data folder (desktop app). The imported database stores paths to lecture recordings, slides or a syllabus that lie outside the folder being imported, or that belong to another lecture or course of it. A library copied to another folder or computer is fine (its paths are moved along); this is about paths the app itself never writes. The app would read those files and could send their text to the AI providers, so the import is refused. "Library" is the user's collection of courses and lectures (资料库), as in the other errors.data_import.*. The end as in the other errors.*: no full stop in the Chinese texts (zh-CN, zh-TW, yue), the sentence-final mark in the others (en: a period).

params.count: how many stored file paths point elsewhere (a number ≥ 1)
params.path: one of those paths as stored, e.g. \\server\share\Week 1.mp4

errors.data_import.network_path.notes: Settings → data folder → import the data folder of the development version (desktop app). The imported database stores paths to lecture recordings or slides on another computer (UNC paths such as \\server\share\…), outside the folder being imported. Opening such a path makes Windows connect to that computer and send the user's sign-in credentials, so the import is refused. The last sentence: when the whole data folder lives on a network share, choosing it by the same path (e.g. the \\server\share\… path rather than a mapped drive letter) makes its paths count as inside it. The end as in the other errors.*: no full stop in the Chinese texts (zh-CN, zh-TW, yue), the sentence-final mark in the others (en: a period).

errors.downloads.local_address.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>). No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed; retrying does not help. A URL of the recording (an entry of its playlist, a redirect, or an address its host name resolves to) is on the user's local network (a private or link-local address, a *.local name) while the page the recording was sent from is on the public internet: LectureFlow refuses so that a web page cannot make it send requests inside the user's own network (security review). Recordings whose page is itself inside the network (a school's server reached over VPN) are not refused. “Local network” = the LAN at home or at school, not the internet.

params.host: the refused host name or IP address, e.g. 127.0.0.1 or localhost

A URL of the recording leads to this computer itself (127.0.0.1, localhost, or a name that resolves to it): never fetched, whatever the page (security review: a web page must not make LectureFlow send requests to programs running on the user's computer).

Shown by the extension when a send is refused, and under a fetch task row on the course page if a playlist or redirect led to such a site. Wording by the lead (plain, not preachy); the extension's errSiteBlocked is the same sentence. Complete sentence with a period.

params.host: the refused host name, every character outside plain ASCII written as %XX, e.g. you%C2%ADtube.com or a;b.example; for an address that is neither http nor https, its scheme and host, e.g. ftp://files.example

errors.downloads.unusual_host.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>). No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed. An address the recording's playlist (or a redirect) leads to has a host name no real site uses (Unicode letters, invisible characters, percent signs, punctuation such as ; or *, two dots in a row); LectureFlow cannot tell which site such a name really reaches, so it refuses it (security review). The same text when a redirect leads to an address that is not a web address at all (ftp://…): LectureFlow only fetches http and https, and {host} is then that address's scheme and host. The text deliberately suggests no remedy: sending the lecture again from the extension would bring the same playlist and fail the same way. “Address” = a web address (URL); “playlist” = the list of media files a recording page serves.

params.scheme: the scheme of the proxy that is set, lower case, e.g. socks5, socks5h or https

errors.downloads.proxy_unsupported.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>). No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed; retrying fails the same way until the proxy setting is changed and LectureFlow is restarted (environment variables are read when it starts), hence no “retry” in the text. The user's proxy (the HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables, which LectureFlow reads like other programs; or ALL_PROXY when the variable of the address's own protocol is not set and NO_PROXY does not exclude the host) is a SOCKS proxy (socks5://, socks5h://, socks4://) or one written with https://. Setting both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY to an http:// proxy makes ALL_PROXY irrelevant, hence the advice to set both. The bundled fetch tool aria2c can only use a plain http:// proxy: with a SOCKS proxy it would silently connect directly, past the proxy, showing the recording's server the user's own address; to an https:// proxy it would send the proxy's password unencrypted. So LectureFlow stops before fetching anything. HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, http:// and aria2c are literal names: keep them untranslated.

errors.selfupdate.untrusted_dir.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”), security review: the data folder lets other accounts of this computer change files (typical when it was moved to a drive such as D:\, where every signed-in account may modify new folders). LectureFlow then neither downloads nor installs updates from it, because another account could swap the files. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. “Diagnostics” (诊断) is the page #/system, where the data folder row offers “Restrict access”. No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

params.path: absolute path of the installation folder or of the item found (not shown)
params.who: account names as Windows reports them, comma-separated (e.g. “Authenticated Users”), or “not confirmed: …” in English; keep as they are

errors.selfupdate.untrusted_install_dir.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”), security audit: LectureFlow was installed in a folder other accounts of this computer can change (typical for a folder made on a drive such as D:\), so the in-app update neither downloads nor installs anything; the user installs the new version by hand from the releases page. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. “Diagnostics” (诊断) is the page #/system; its row “Installation folder” (common.check.install_dir: use the same words) says what to do about the folder. No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

params.version: the version of the update that waits, e.g. 3.2.1
params.kind: which copy the update belongs to, already in the UI language: the text of errors.selfupdate.copy_installer (“安装版 / the installed one”) or errors.selfupdate.copy_portable (“便携版 / the portable one”); it must read well where {kind} stands in this sentence

errors.selfupdate.other_copy_pending.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”), Settings > App > App updates: shown under the status after the user clicked Download, or under the “update from files” drop zone. The same account can have two copies of LectureFlow that use the same data folder: the one set up by the installer and the portable one. Each takes its own kind of package, and the data folder holds only one prepared update at a time. Here the other copy has one ready (downloaded, or brought in from files; it installs it the next time it is started), so this copy does not start its own, which would replace it. What the user does: close this copy, start the other one (it installs the update and comes up again), then come back and update this copy. Say “ready / prepared”, not “downloaded”. The last sentence: the other copy may no longer exist, so after 14 days without that update being installed this copy no longer waits and can be updated again; keep the number 14 (the back end's rule). “This copy / this one” = the LectureFlow the user is looking at. “Data folder” as in the other strings (数据目录). No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

errors.selfupdate.copy_installer.notes: Not an error of its own: a short name put into errors.selfupdate.other_copy_pending where {kind} stands, for the copy of LectureFlow that was set up by the installer (as opposed to the portable copy, a single .exe that needs no installation). Lower case in languages with letter case (it stands inside a sentence, in brackets in zh-CN and en); no period.

errors.selfupdate.copy_portable.notes: Not an error of its own: a short name put into errors.selfupdate.other_copy_pending where {kind} stands, for the portable copy of LectureFlow (a single .exe that runs without being installed), as opposed to the one set up by the installer. Lower case in languages with letter case (it stands inside a sentence); no period.

errors.selfupdate.no_manifest.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates, under the line settings.update.state.no_manifest: a check reached GitHub (or a mirror), but the latest release has no update.json or no update.json.minisig yet (HTTP 404). This is what users see between the moment a new version is published and the moment the maintainer uploads its signature, usually a few hours. Say clearly that it is not the user's network (the older text for unreachable sources asked them to check it). LectureFlow checks again by itself after about 2 hours when automatic checks are on; the next line says when. update.json is a file name: keep it. No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

errors.angle.not_found.notes: Second camera angle (第二视角): a lecture can keep a second, video-only recording of another camera (from the extension's “dual camera” option, or added on the lecture page). {name} is the angle's internal name (angle2).

errors.angle.no_video.notes: Second camera angle (第二视角): a lecture can keep a second, video-only recording of another camera (from the extension's “dual camera” option, or added on the lecture page). The file the user picked has only audio.

errors.angle.remux_failed.notes: Second camera angle (第二视角): a lecture can keep a second, video-only recording of another camera (from the extension's “dual camera” option, or added on the lecture page). The file is copied into an MP4 without re-encoding; this fails for codecs MP4 cannot hold or for files that are not video. Details carry ffmpeg's message.

errors.check.credentials_key_missing.notes: Detail of the credentials check on the diagnostics page (#/system), a warning (test-upgrade F6): the key file secrets.key was not in the data folder, so a new key was made; what was encrypted with the old key is kept but cannot be read. Keep the file name secrets.key as is.

params.dir: absolute path of the data folder

errors.check.hint_credentials_restore_ke.notes: Fix hint of the credentials check on Windows while saved credentials cannot be decrypted (test-upgrade F6). Keep the file names secrets.key and secrets.key.unreadable-restored exactly: LectureFlow looks for files named secrets.key.unreadable-* and opens the ones that still decrypt. “Re-enter key” is settings.provider.key_unreadable_chip; “Settings → Providers” must match the settings page.

errors.check.credentials_scrub_pending.notes: Detail of the credentials check on the diagnostics page (#/system), a warning (test-upgrade F9): the credentials are encrypted, but the step that wipes old values from the database file (compacting it and emptying its write-ahead log) has not completed, usually because another program was reading the database.

errors.check.hint_credentials_scrub_pend.notes: Fix hint for errors.check.credentials_scrub_pending: nothing to do but restart; if it stays, close programs that keep the database file open. Keep the file name lectureflow.db.

params.path: absolute path of the data folder
params.max: the longest data folder path that works on any computer (a number)
params.hard: the length beyond which the processes cannot start at all, long path support or not (a number, larger than {max})

errors.check.data_dir_path_too_long_to_s.notes: Detail of the data folder location check (#/system), a warning, Windows only (test-upgrade F10, R6-E): the data folder path is longer than {hard} (258 − 72). The processes of transcription, fixing sentence breaks (common.action.rerun_text_only) and slide text extraction (stage.material_extract) are started in the lecture and slide folders, 71 and 72 characters below the data folder (“about 70”), and Windows refuses a working folder longer than 258 characters whatever the long path setting (measured; at {hard} + 1 the slide folders, one more the lecture folders too): keep this part unconditional. The second part is errors.check.data_dir_path_too_long's (worked out from the code, hence “may”): a folder just shortened to within {hard} is not enough. Name all three steps.

params.path: absolute path of the data folder
params.max: the longest data folder path that works on any computer (a number)

errors.check.data_dir_path_too_long.notes: Detail of the data folder location check (#/system), a warning, Windows only (test-upgrade F10, R6-E), for a path longer than {max} but not than errors.check.data_dir_path_too_long_to_start's limit: transcription and fixing sentence breaks (common.action.rerun_text_only) work in the lecture folders, slide text extraction (stage.material_extract) in the slide folders; the files their workers read and write lie up to 94 characters below the data folder (“about 90”). Without Windows long path support (off by default; on Windows it is the “Win32 long paths” setting) such a worker cannot open a path longer than 259 characters, so {max} is 259 − 94. What fails first beyond it depends on the file, hence “may”; the limit is worked out from the code and was not reproduced on a computer without long path support: do not say it was measured or observed. Name all three steps.

params.path: absolute path of the data folder
params.max: the longest data folder path that works on any computer (a number)

errors.check.data_dir_path_near_limit.notes: Same check, a warning: the data folder path is within 10 characters of that limit. Name the three steps (transcription, fixing sentence breaks, slide text extraction) and the long path support as in errors.check.data_dir_path_too_long; not measured either.

errors.check.hint_data_dir_shorter.notes: Fix hint for the three path length details.“Settings → Data folder” must match the settings page, as in errors.check.hint_data_dir_move; keep D:\LectureFlow as the example.

params.path: absolute path of the data folder
params.max: the longest data folder path under which all the components named after it can be installed (a number; with the current components 81 for gcloud, 96 for NVIDIA GPU transcription, 108 for the Python runtime, 110 for Intel transcription)

errors.check.data_dir_path_components.notes: Detail of the data folder location check (#/system), a warning, Windows only (T27 P2). Some components this computer needs are not installed, and under a data folder longer than {max} their deepest file would get a path longer than 250 characters, the limit the components keep to (errors.components.path_too_long, whose {max} is that 250), so the component manager refuses to install them. The components follow as clauses of their own, one per component, each naming it and what needs it (errors.check.data_dir_component_*; joined with the language's clause separator, or as new sentences when they start with a capital letter): end this text so that such clauses can follow, and do not list components here. Do not promise a way out (Colab, for one, needs gcloud, which may be one of the components that cannot be installed). Comes before errors.check.data_dir_cloud_sync and the other path length details; its hint is errors.check.hint_data_dir_shorter, or errors.check.hint_data_dir_move when the folder is also in a sync folder or on a disk without permissions.

errors.check.data_dir_component_python.notes: A clause after errors.check.data_dir_path_components: the Python runtime (compui.name.python; keep that name and the quotes) cannot be installed in this data folder. Every transcription component on this computer depends on it, and the slide text extraction (stage.material_extract) runs with it. Not shown when the user set up a Python of their own.

errors.check.data_dir_component_asr_cuda.notes: A clause after errors.check.data_dir_path_components: NVIDIA GPU transcription (compui.name.asr_cuda; keep that name and the quotes) cannot be installed in this data folder, and it is the transcription the hardware recommendation picks for this computer (it has an NVIDIA GPU).

errors.check.data_dir_component_asr_open.notes: A clause after errors.check.data_dir_path_components: Intel transcription (compui.name.asr_openvino; keep that name and the quotes) cannot be installed in this data folder, and the hardware recommendation picks it for this computer (an Intel GPU or NPU, or transcription on the CPU alone).

errors.check.data_dir_component_gcloud.notes: A clause after errors.check.data_dir_path_components, shown only when Colab is set up and in use: the Google Cloud CLI (compui.name.gcloud; keep that name and the quotes) cannot be installed in this data folder, and signing in to Colab inside LectureFlow runs it. Not shown when a gcloud of the user's own is on PATH.

params.added: file names of slides that now apply to the lecture (a list: each name already in settings.quote, joined by common.list_sep)
params.removed: file names of slides that no longer apply (a list, each name quoted)

stale.reason.materials_changed.notes: Why stages are out of date: the set of slides a lecture uses changed (slides bound to its teaching week, to it, or course-wide) — e.g. after the term start, a recording time or a slide binding changed. Same wording family as stale.reason.material_changed. The code quotes each file name itself: do not put quotation marks around {added} or {removed}.

params.added: file names of slides that now apply (a list, each name quoted)

stale.reason.materials_changed_added.notes: As stale.reason.materials_changed, only slides were added.

params.removed: file names of slides that no longer apply (a list, each name quoted)

stale.reason.materials_changed_removed.notes: As stale.reason.materials_changed, only slides were removed.

stale.reason.materials_changed_plain.notes: As stale.reason.materials_changed when the earlier set is not known (no file names).

params.text: reason recorded before v2, shown as it is

params.reasons: one or more stale reasons joined with common.clause_sep: the first as at the start of a sentence, the next ones in their stale.reason_inline form
params.stages: list of stage names (catalog words only, never a file name: {stages:lc} is fine)

stale.need_update.notes: Shown on a lecture row and the lecture page. Keep {reasons} at the start and without :lc (see stale.reason_inline).

params.reason: stale reason

stale.card.notes: In the card of a stale stage.

params.reason: one stale reason (a stale.reason.* text) as it reads at the start of a sentence

stale.reason_inline.notes: A stale reason in mid-sentence: every reason after the first where several are joined with common.clause_sep (stale.need_update), and every reason after the label of course.confirm.update_why. Write {reason} to keep it as it is (zh-CN, en, and the languages without letter case). Russian writes {reason:lc}, so the reason's own words start in lower case ("Почему нужно обновить: изменились слайды…"). The file names and the recorded texts a reason carries stay as written whatever the modifier; never put :lc on {reasons} or {reason} in stale.need_update, stale.card or course.confirm.update_why (it would reach those names).

waiting.on_battery.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: battery awareness keeps the NVIDIA card idle on battery (waiting_for on_battery).

waiting.memory.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: an Intel device needs more system memory than is free (waiting_for memory).

waiting.no_asr_device.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: no device is turned on and detected (waiting_for no_asr_device). 'Transcription' is the settings section name (settings.block.asr).

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost"), not translated

waiting.device_selftest.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: its device runs a device test (waiting_for device_selftest:{id}).

waiting.power_wait_ac.notes: What a transcription stage waits for (waiting_for power_wait_ac): on battery, a transcription of a device that is not used on battery (e.g. the NVIDIA GPU) continues on that device when the power adapter is connected. Keep the "<status>: power-aware - <reason>" structure of the source. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.power_no_saver_device.notes: waiting_for power_no_saver_device: on battery neither an NPU nor an Intel GPU is turned on and detected (the NVIDIA GPU and the CPU are never used on battery). Also the resource monitor's note when no device is active. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.power_no_device.notes: waiting_for power_no_device: a laptop plugged in has no NVIDIA GPU or Intel GPU turned on and detected (or none of the devices chosen by hand); a laptop never transcribes on the CPU. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

waiting.power_queue.notes: waiting_for power_queue:{id}: the one active device of a laptop is busy; the task is not given to another device. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.from: the device running now (name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated))
params.to: the device chosen for the new power state

waiting.power_switch_pending.notes: waiting_for power_switch_pending:{from}:{to}: e.g. the charger was plugged in while the NPU runs a lecture; plugging in never interrupts a transcription, the next one starts on the new device. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

waiting.power_device_selftest.notes: waiting_for device_selftest:{id} on a laptop (one active device at a time): the active device runs a device test, the task waits for it instead of going to another device. On a desktop waiting.device_selftest is shown. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.remote_queue.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_window.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_auth.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_balance.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_busy.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when only Google Colab can take it and Colab is busy with another lecture (Colab transcribes one lecture at a time) or is still starting or shutting down; it starts by itself when Colab is free. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_fallback.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after Google Colab handed the lecture back (notes.remote.back_to_local is shown next to it) while this computer has no transcription device that could take it: it would wait for good. The stage card offers the button common.action.use_colab (= menu.lecture.use_colab, “Process on Colab instead”); the second part points to it without quoting it exactly. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts.

waiting.remote_held.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after the user pressed one of the Colab shutdown buttons (resources.remote.after_current “Shut down after this lecture” / resources.remote.now “Shut down now”): sending lectures to Colab automatically stays paused while lectures wait (resources.remote.held), and this computer has no transcription device that could take the lecture, so it would wait until the user acts. The stage card offers the button common.action.use_colab (= menu.lecture.use_colab, “Process on Colab instead”), which also ends the pause; the second part points to it without quoting it exactly. “As you asked” = the pause is the user's own choice, not a fault. Same style as waiting.remote_fallback: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts. zh-CN addresses the user as 你, like the rest of the interface.

waiting.no_provider.notes: What a stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) in the “Transcription only” setup (3.1.0; onboarding.tier.transcribe_only.*): correction, translation and the summary need a model service and wait until one is set up in Settings, then continue by themselves. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period. “Model service” = what onboarding calls a service (an API provider).

waiting.remote_offline.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it may run only on the user's own SSH inference servers (Settings → Remote servers; ssh-mvp) and the server cannot be reached now: LectureFlow is connecting or reconnecting; it starts by itself when the server is back. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_setup.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it may run only on the user's own SSH inference servers (Settings → Remote servers; ssh-mvp) and the server is reachable but its transcription environment (Python packages and the Whisper model) is not installed yet or is being installed. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_fallback_ssh.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after one of the user's own SSH inference servers handed the lecture back (it is never sent to a remote device automatically again) while this computer has no transcription device that could take it. The Colab counterpart is waiting.remote_fallback. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.component_missing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for component_missing:{id}): this computer has the device, but the software it needs to transcribe (a component such as “NVIDIA GPU transcription”, installed under Settings → Components, the settings section settings.comp.title) is not installed yet, typically right after a fresh install. The lecture waits and starts on its own once the component is installed; nothing to retry. Same style as waiting.device_paused / waiting.memory: phrase, no period; the colon (zh) or semicolon (en) joins what is missing and what to do. zh-CN addresses the user as 你 (here implicit), like the rest of the interface.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.model_missing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for model_missing:{id}): the device's transcription software is installed, but the Whisper model chosen for that device (its model setting in the transcription device settings, settings.block.asr) is not installed as a component. Two ways out: install that model under Settings → Components, or switch the device to a model that is installed (its model setting under Transcription in the settings). The lecture then starts on its own. Same style as waiting.component_missing: phrase, no period.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.component_installing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for component_installing:{id}): the component the device needs (its transcription software or its model) is being downloaded or installed right now (also while that download is paused); the lecture starts on the device once it is done. Neutral, no urgency. Phrase, no period, like waiting.device_slot.

waiting.retry_backoff_due.notes: What a stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) once the countdown of waiting.retry_backoff ('Retrying automatically in {n} seconds') has reached zero: the automatic retry starts within a second, or as soon as a slot is free. Also the {wait} of common.summary.failed_wait ('{stage} failed. {wait}').

player.menu.reset_hint.notes: Sentence context menu (player transcript, and the transcript tab of the lecture page): grey hint next to the Restore item. Round 8: what Restore does — it drops the sentence's human text, whether it came from an edit or from accepting or rejecting a correction, and the sentence shows the correction stage's text again (修复结果 = corrected text, glossary; internal/state review.go ResetSentence, text = COALESCE(human_text, repaired_text)). It is not a step-by-step undo. en says “AI-corrected” so that “corrected” is not read as the user's own correction (T23 general 7); zh “修复” already names that stage.

Same wording as common.model_choice.current.

player.edit.label.notes: Player: sentence edit dialog field label (the text box's accessible name). Round 8 (C175b): the same word as the dialog title player.edit.title and the menu item player.menu.edit (glossary: 原文 = English sentence).

player.edit.hint_held.notes: Player: sentence edit dialog hint while the lecture's translation is out of date, failed or cancelled (R78b medium 2); otherwise player.edit.hint.

player.edit.zh_note.notes: Under the English sentence being edited (player edit dialog, lecture page inline edit) while the lecture's translation is done or running (T22 S2, T23 general 7, R74 medium 1, R78b medium 2). There is no way to edit a translation directly. While it is held, player.edit.zh_note_held. Round 8 (I68): the last sentence is about English edits made in the period after a term's translation is set in the glossary and before “Update”; name that period, not “before that” (which can be read as before setting the term).

player.edit.zh_note_held.notes: Under the English sentence being edited while the lecture's translation is out of date, failed or cancelled: edits are translated only when the translation runs again (R78b medium 2). Round 9 (TX-02, T28 suggestion 4): it comes right after player.edit.hint_held (player dialog) or transcript.edit.hint_held (lecture page), which already say that the lecture's translation must run again first (“Update” of the whole lecture, or a retry of the translation). Do not say that sentence again: only refer to it briefly (“the translation must run again first”), then say what is this note's own: the translation itself cannot be edited; until that run, editing the English sentence or translating the sentence again only marks it, and it is translated in that run; “Update” of the whole lecture runs the out-of-date stages again and bills them again. On the lecture page a busy lecture shows a busy text instead of the hint, so the note must also make sense alone.

player.edit.saved_held.notes: After saving a sentence edit while the lecture's translation is out of date, failed or cancelled (R78b medium 2); otherwise player.edit.saved.

course.confirm.launch_cost_transcribe_on.notes: Instead of course.confirm.launch_cost in the Start all drafts confirmation when no model service is set up for summary, correction and translation (the “Transcription only” setup, onboarding.tier.transcribe_only.name): those stages send nothing now and wait until a service is added in Settings (waiting.no_provider). Do not promise that nothing costs money (remote transcription may). Round 9 (TX-09, R86 I6): it no longer starts with the setup's name. launchCostMode (update_confirm.js) picks this sentence when none of the three lecture roles (summary, correction, translation) has a service, even if the outline or glossary roles have one, so it says that these three have no model service, not that none is set up at all, and that they wait until a service is set up for them (a service may already exist for other roles; waiting.no_provider); written like course.confirm.launch_cost and launch_cost_free, which also start with the three stages.

course.confirm.launch_cost_free.notes: Instead of course.confirm.launch_cost in the Start all drafts confirmation when the providers of summary, correction and translation all have their prices set to 0 (e.g. free quotas): requests are still sent, and the provider may charge after all (a quota used up, prices it changed), so “may cost money”, not “billed by use” nor “free”. Same sentence shape as course.confirm.launch_cost.

lecture.stat.tokens_total_sub.notes: Round 7 (T25 S1): under the token stat (whose large figure is the sum of each stage's last run) when the back end gives the lecture's total over every task and attempt: first the total, then that the figure above is the last runs (R72 M4: the line is one line, cut with an ellipsis in a narrow cell, so the number must come first). Replaces lecture.stat.tokens_sub then. Hover: lecture.stat.usage_tip. Round 8 (I61, I63, I67): no fixed limit, the text is cut or wrapped by the display. Measured on the mock (11 px): in a window wider than a phone the cell is one line, cut with an ellipsis, and holds about 19 Chinese / 26 Latin / 22 Cyrillic / 25 Devanagari characters of it at the narrowest six-column layout (1100 px window), about 25 / 40 / 33 / 37 at 1280 px; at phone width (360 px) it wraps onto 3–4 lines and nothing is cut. So keep the total first and the explanation after it, which may be cut (the hover, lecture.stat.usage_tip, explains both figures).

params.total: formatted amount over every run of the lecture, e.g. ¥0.27

lecture.stat.cost_total_sub.notes: Round 7 (T25 S1): under the estimated cost (each stage's last run) when the lecture's total over every run is known; replaces lecture.stat.cost_sub then. Use the same words as lecture.stat.tokens_total_sub, the amount first (R72 M4). Round 8 (I61, I63, I67): no fixed limit, cut or wrapped by the display as lecture.stat.tokens_total_sub (measured: about 16 Chinese / 26 Latin / 22 Cyrillic / 23 Devanagari characters visible at the narrowest six-column layout, the whole text at 1280 px except ru; 2–4 lines at phone width).

lecture.stat.usage_tip.notes: Round 7 (T25 S1): hover of the token and cost stats on the lecture page when the total is shown: why the large figure (each stage's last run) can go down, and what the total (“累计”, the word of lecture.stat.cost_total_sub) includes.

lecture.notice.stream_generating.notes: Lecture page notice while the playback file (browser-playable video) is made in the background after preprocessing (stream-parallel: the video needed converting, which takes minutes). Must make clear that the transcript work is not waiting for it and that the player can already play the audio. Updated live.

lecture.notice.stream_failed.notes: Lecture page notice, bold start: the playback file (browser-playable video) could not be made; the reason follows (an errors.media.* text or the restart interruption), with a Retry button. The transcript is not affected; the player plays the audio.

lecture.notice.stream_cancelled.notes: Lecture page notice, bold: the user cancelled making the playback file (browser-playable video); a Retry button follows. The transcript is not affected.

lecture.notice.split.notes: Lecture page, a quiet notice under the pipeline: the transcription ran in “极速模式” (fast mode, settings.colab.fast_label) on Colab. Fragment, no period.

lecture.notice.power_wait.notes: Round 7 (T24 S4): lecture page notice while the power-aware policy holds the transcription on battery (the status beside the bar says “挂起：电源感知 - …”, waiting.power_*): what ends the wait. Used for power_no_saver_device when no Intel graphics or NPU could take over but a device would on mains power, and for the old on_battery; see lecture.notice.power_wait_other, power_wait_ac, power_enable_saver, power_no_device (R72 H1: one text per case of the power policy). A button lecture.notice.power_settings follows.

lecture.notice.power_wait_other.notes: Round 7 (T24 S4): as lecture.notice.power_wait, for power_no_saver_device only (R72 H1: never for a run bound to the NVIDIA GPU, power_wait_ac), when an Intel graphics device or an NPU is present but turned off: turned on in Settings (section “转写”, settings.block.asr; quote it as that key is translated), it can transcribe on battery. The policy itself is the user's choice and stays; this only says the way out.

lecture.notice.power_wait_ac.notes: R72 H1: lecture page notice for waiting_for power_wait_ac (“挂起：电源感知 - 等待电源适配器”): on battery the run is bound to a device that is not the battery device — a pinned model, or a checkpoint made on the NVIDIA GPU, which the power policy never hands to the Intel graphics or the NPU. Only plugging in ends the wait; turning on another device does not, so the text must not suggest it.

lecture.notice.power_enable_saver.notes: R72 H1: notice for power_no_saver_device when no NVIDIA GPU or Intel graphics is usable on mains power either, while an Intel graphics device or NPU is present but turned off: turning it on (section “转写”, settings.block.asr) lets the transcription go on, on battery too.

lecture.notice.power_no_device.notes: R72 H1: notice for power_no_device (on mains power, no usable NVIDIA GPU or Intel graphics; the CPU is never used on a laptop): plugging in is no way out; a device turned on in Settings may be. No promise that it then goes on (a lecture pinned to a CPU device would not).

lecture.notice.power_settings.notes: Round 7 (T24 S4): a link styled as a button in the power-wait notice; opens Settings at the transcription section (its device list).

lecture.notice.budget_wait.notes: Round 7 (T24 G3): lecture page notice while a stage waits because today's daily budget (settings.general.budget) is used up: when it resumes by itself (midnight, local time, as resources.budget_hit says) and where to raise the budget now (section “存储与其他”, settings.block.general; quote it as that key is translated). A button lecture.notice.budget_settings follows.

lecture.notice.budget_settings.notes: Round 7 (T24 G3): a link styled as a button in the budget notice; opens Settings at the section with the daily budget. A verb first, as other buttons (R72 L5).

lecture.text_repair.title.notes: Title of the confirmation dialog of common.action.rerun_text_only. A question.

lecture.text_repair.message.notes: First paragraph of that dialog: why it is offered (long passages without punctuation or in capitals) and what it does. “Fix sentence breaks” (修复断句, textrepair-int): for a lecture transcribed before LectureFlow learned to repair degenerate Whisper output, the transcript's long runs without punctuation and its all-caps passages are repaired by statistics learned from the same lecture's normal text (full stops added, capitals restored), and the sentences are split again. It does not transcribe the audio again. The four points below it are lecture.text_repair.no_transcribe, keep_reviewed, downstream and patches.

lecture.text_repair.no_transcribe.notes: Point 1 of the dialog (a list item, a complete sentence): the audio is not transcribed again; only the stored text changes; it is quick (seconds).

lecture.text_repair.keep_reviewed.notes: Point 2: sentences the user reviewed and edited by hand (human_text) are kept exactly as they are. Address the user directly (你 / you).

lecture.text_repair.downstream.notes: Point 3: the stages after transcription (summary, AI correction = 修复, the LLM correction stage common.stage.repair, translation and export) become out of date and run again automatically, which costs LLM usage of about 0.2 yuan (CNY, ¥) per lecture; keep the amount and the currency.

lecture.text_repair.patches.notes: Point 4: the review's records of accepting or rejecting the AI correction's suggestions (patches) are cleared; the review starts again from the new suggestions.

lecture.text_repair.ok.notes: Confirm button of that dialog; the same words as common.action.rerun_text_only.

lecture.use_remote.message.notes: Confirmation of the lecture menu item “Process on …” (ssh-1b); its title is the menu item’s text.

lecture.use_remote.done.notes: Toast after a lecture was sent to the SSH remote server {name} (ssh-1b).
