resources.unpriced.notes: Resource monitor provider row and the dashboard usage card: some of today's requests had no price and are not in the estimated cost

resources.title.notes: Title of the resource monitor (right column)

resources.offline.notes: Resource panel head, in place of resources.live while the connection to the service is lost.

resources.offline_tip.notes: Hover text of resources.offline and of the collapsed panel's numbers (shown as “--”) while the connection is lost.

resources.offline_note.notes: Resource panel body while the connection to the service is lost (the readings of before are not shown).

resources.gpu.switch.notes: Switch that pauses or resumes GPU jobs

resources.gpu.running.notes: Label next to the switch (narrow column)

resources.gpu.paused.notes: Label next to the switch (narrow column)

resources.devices.switch.notes: Main switch of the resource panel's transcription section: pauses or resumes every device.

resources.devices.pause_all_title.notes: Title of the dialog asked before pausing every device while transcriptions run (its message is nav.gpu.pause_message).

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost"), not translated

resources.devices.device_switch.notes: Switch on one device card: pauses or resumes that device only.

resources.devices.idle.notes: A device card without running tasks.

resources.devices.battery_mode.notes: Tag on a device card while the computer runs on battery (SPEC-v2 I10).

resources.devices.battery_mode_tip.notes: Hover text of the tag "Battery · power-aware" on the active device card and of the power line while a laptop runs on battery: the battery rules of the power-aware policy. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.devices.util_na.notes: Hover text of “--” in the usage tile of an Intel device.

resources.devices.temp_na.notes: Hover text of “--” in the temperature tile of an Intel device card (no Windows counter reports it without administrator rights).

resources.devices.apple_mem.notes: Row label on the Apple GPU's card in the resource bar (mac-opti M6): how much of the unified memory the GPU holds, shown against the installed memory (e.g. 1.6 GB / 16 GB).

resources.system.title.notes: Upper section of the resource monitor: CPU, memory, CPU temperature and the power state the power-aware policy follows.

resources.system.cpu.notes: Tile label (narrow, half of the monitor's width): total CPU usage in percent.

resources.system.mem.notes: Row label: physical memory used / installed (e.g. 14.2 GB / 31.7 GB). Also used as the label of an Intel device's shared GPU memory on its card (used / available, e.g. 2.9 GB / 15.8 GB).

resources.system.cpu_temp.notes: Tile label (narrow): the highest thermal zone temperature; "--" when the computer reports none.

resources.system.unified_mem.notes: Resource bar, upper area, on Apple silicon (mac-opti M6): replaces resources.system.mem; the memory used / installed is the unified memory the CPU and GPU share (Activity Monitor's “Memory Used”).

resources.system.stream_bg_one.notes: Resource panel, system area: one lecture's playback file (browser-playable video) is being converted in the background, in parallel with transcription.

resources.system.stream_bg_many.notes: Resource panel, system area: several lectures' playback files are being converted in the background at the same time. n is always 2 or more.

resources.system.stream_bg_tip.notes: Hover text of the background playback-file line in the resource panel: why it runs separately and that it does not use a transcription device (GPU/NPU slot), only one CPU slot.

resources.power.ac.notes: Power source in the resource monitor: external power (power adapter or USB-C; they cannot be told apart reliably).

resources.power.battery.notes: Power source in the resource monitor: running on battery.

resources.power.level.notes: Battery charge next to the power source.

resources.power.charging.notes: Tag next to the power source: the battery is charging.

resources.power.not_charging.notes: Tag next to the power source while plugged in: the battery is not charging (e.g. full).

resources.power.no_battery.notes: Tag next to the power source of a desktop: no battery, so the power-aware rules do not apply.

resources.power.basis_tip.notes: Hover text of the power row: this is the state the power-aware device choice follows.

resources.power.wait_ac.notes: Line in the power section: transcriptions suspended on battery until the power adapter is connected. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.power.wait_no_device.notes: Line in the power section: transcriptions suspended because no device qualifies under the power-aware rules. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.power.wait_way_out.notes: Resource panel, power section: under the notes of transcription tasks the power-aware policy suspended on battery (resources.power.wait_ac, wait_no_device): what happens next and the way not to wait; the link resources.power.to_settings follows. The policy itself is deliberate, not a fault.

resources.power.to_settings.notes: Resource panel, power section: link after resources.power.wait_way_out to the transcription devices block of Settings.

resources.devices.suspended_label.notes: Resource panel: the label beside the main switch of the transcription devices (on) while the power-aware policy holds every task and nothing runs; otherwise the switch says common.status.running or devices.paused.

resources.active.title.notes: Middle section of the resource monitor: the device(s) the power-aware policy uses now (cards), with the main pause switch.

resources.power.reason.ac_auto.notes: Tag on the active device card: why this device — plugged in, chosen automatically (NVIDIA GPU, else Intel GPU).

resources.power.reason.battery.notes: Tag on the active device card: why this device — on battery, the power-aware choice (NPU, else Intel GPU).

resources.power.reason.manual.notes: Tag on the active device card: the device is in the list chosen in Settings (Transcription device: choose devices yourself).

resources.power.reason.desktop.notes: Tag on the device cards of a computer where no battery is detected — a desktop, or a laptop whose power state cannot be read: the device list's order, several devices at once. Must not say "desktop": a laptop with an unknown power state gets it too.

resources.power.reason.switch_pending.notes: Tag on the active device card instead of the reason tag when the charger was plugged in (or the preferred device changed) while this device runs a lecture: it finishes the lecture, then the preferred device takes over (hover: resources.power.next). Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

resources.power.next.notes: Note on the active card after the charger was plugged in (or unplugged): the running lecture finishes here, the next one starts on {device}. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.power.manual_ignored.notes: Note in the middle section: devices are chosen in Settings, but on battery the power-aware choice applies.

resources.standby.title.notes: Bottom section of the resource monitor: the devices not in use now, one row each; a row opens its details.

resources.standby.standby.notes: Tag of a device row: turned on, not used now (the power-aware policy uses another device).

resources.standby.untested.notes: Small tag of a device row: the device test has never run on it.

resources.standby.holds_suspended.notes: Tag of a device row: a transcription suspended by the power-aware policy continues on this device when plugged in.

resources.rail.asr_power.notes: Collapsed monitor, while the power-aware policy suspends transcriptions.

resources.balance_failed.notes: Used when the reason has no translation of its own

params.when: relative time, such as “3 minutes ago”

resources.col.cache_hit.notes: Column header: cache hit rate (narrow column)

resources.missing_holidays.notes: Note in a provider row of the resource monitor

dashboard.retried_partial.notes: Result of the dashboard's “Retry all” when some failures were left out or refused; written like dashboard.launched_partial and dashboard.updated_partial.

dashboard.retry_skip.model.notes: Clause of dashboard.retried_partial: failures that a plain retry cannot get past (the model refused, the time limit of one request); quote common.action.retry_model exactly. Round 8 (R76 L-12): the workbench row of each such failure has that button itself, so the text names no page. Round 9 (TX-06, I77): it goes into dashboard.retried_partial's {reason} (view_dashboard.js, U.clauseJoin), the clauses in this order: model, futile, no_action, then the errors of refused requests (dashboard.retry_skip.cancelled among them), joined by common.clause_sep. Where retried_partial puts {reason} after a full stop (en “Not retried: {n}. {reason}”, also ru and hi), the first clause starts a sentence and the others follow the separator. Start with {n} (the number), as ru does, so that the clause reads in both places; never start it with a lower-case word.

dashboard.retry_skip.futile.notes: Clause of dashboard.retried_partial: lectures whose media file is damaged (errors.media.corrupt); a retry reads the same file, so they are left out. Round 9 (TX-06, I77): it goes into dashboard.retried_partial's {reason} (view_dashboard.js, U.clauseJoin), the clauses in this order: model, futile, no_action, then the errors of refused requests (dashboard.retry_skip.cancelled among them), joined by common.clause_sep. Where retried_partial puts {reason} after a full stop (en “Not retried: {n}. {reason}”, also ru and hi), the first clause starts a sentence and the others follow the separator. Start with {n} (the number), as ru does, so that the clause reads in both places; never start it with a lower-case word.

dashboard.retry_skip.cancelled.notes: Clause of dashboard.retried_partial: the model question of “Retry all” (the models recorded differ from the settings) was cancelled, so those failures were not retried. Round 9 (TX-06, I77): it goes into dashboard.retried_partial's {reason} (view_dashboard.js, U.clauseJoin) after the model, futile and no_action clauses (when there are any), among the errors of other refused requests, joined by common.clause_sep. So it may come first (where retried_partial puts {reason} after a full stop, en “Not retried: {n}. {reason}”, also ru and hi, it then starts a sentence) or after the separator behind other clauses (“…; No model was chosen”): write a short clause that reads in both places. It has no {n} and is shown once, however many lectures it concerns.

dashboard.retry_skip.no_action.notes: Clause of dashboard.retried_partial: failures for which the server offers no retry right now (rare), so “Retry all” left them out; their lecture pages say what can be done. Written like dashboard.retry_skip.futile. Round 9 (TX-06, I77): it goes into dashboard.retried_partial's {reason} (view_dashboard.js, U.clauseJoin), the clauses in this order: model, futile, no_action, then the errors of refused requests (dashboard.retry_skip.cancelled among them), joined by common.clause_sep. Where retried_partial puts {reason} after a full stop (en “Not retried: {n}. {reason}”, also ru and hi), the first clause starts a sentence and the others follow the separator. Start with {n} (the number), as ru does, so that the clause reads in both places; never start it with a lower-case word.

dashboard.colab.leftover_session_title.notes: Round 8: title of the same workbench warning when the leftover is an earlier Colab session that cannot be released because the authorization has ended (colab.leftover_session; the text below is resources.remote.leftover_session_any or errors.colab.leftover_session). LectureFlow does not know whether it still runs (those texts say “may”; do not claim it runs or has stopped). Round 9 (TX-07, R87 section 4): the text below starts with “An earlier Colab session may still be running”, so the title no longer says that; it says what is needed instead: LectureFlow can release the session only after the user authorizes again (importing a new authorization releases it on its own, internal/colab backend.go ImportADCFile → cleanupLeftover). The text below also says it can be stopped on the Colab website, so the title need not claim that authorizing is the only way. en is written as an instruction to stay within max 40 (R89 low 3); the text right below names the Colab session.

settings.provider.rate_limits.observed.notes: Provider dialog (Anthropic type at api.anthropic.com only), under the concurrency and per-minute fields. Anthropic's limits are per model class: say it is this model's limit, as observed in the response headers of recent answers since the app started (the model with the smallest limit used in the last 24 hours), not a promise and not “your account's limit” in general. Followed on the same line by settings.provider.rate_limits.tokens (when known), the suggestion and settings.provider.rate_limits.caveat.

settings.provider.rate_limits.advice.notes: The suggestion from the observed limit, shown in the provider dialog and in the provider row's banner when the current settings are clearly below it. The app never applies it by itself.

params.max: suggested number of requests at a time (1–32)

settings.provider.rate_limits.advice_unl.notes: As settings.provider.rate_limits.advice when the provider has no per-minute limit: that stays so; only the concurrency is suggested.

settings.provider.rate_limits.caveat.notes: Last sentence of the observed-limits text in the provider dialog. Must stay honest: the number is observed, not guaranteed, and the suggestion is deliberately cautious (it uses about 60% of the limit).

settings.provider.rate_limits.none.notes: Provider dialog of an existing Anthropic provider at api.anthropic.com (https), before any answer of this run reported its limits (they are not stored; after a restart they come back with the next request). Worded like settings.provider.rate_limits.observed: the limit is the model's, as observed, not “the account's actual limits”. No request is sent to learn them; not shown for other hosts (they never report limits here).

settings.provider.rate_limits.fill.notes: Small button. In the provider dialog it only puts the suggestion into the concurrency and per-minute fields; the user still has to click Save. In the provider row's banner it opens that dialog with the suggestion filled in. Never “apply”/“save” wording.

settings.provider.rate_limits.filled.notes: Announced (role=status) next to settings.provider.rate_limits.fill after the fields were filled: nothing is saved until the user clicks the dialog's Save (common.save).

settings.provider.rate_limits.estimated.notes: After the suggestion in the provider dialog when no successful answer has been measured yet (only the request limit is known, e.g. the first answer seen was a 429): the suggestion ignores the token limits and assumes 3 seconds a request. No banner is shown in that case.

settings.provider.rate_limits.gradual.notes: Last sentence of the provider dialog's limits text when a suggestion is shown. From Anthropic's rate limit documentation: limits may be enforced over shorter intervals (60 per minute as 1 per second), and a sharp increase in usage can trigger acceleration limits (HTTP 429). Keep “429”.

The limit is the model's (per model class), as observed, not a promise. Followed by settings.provider.rate_limits.advice / advice_unlimited and the button settings.provider.rate_limits.fill. This variant: only the concurrency is low (the per-minute limit is fine or unlimited: never mention it here).

params.model: the model id the limit was reported for, verbatim (e.g. claude-opus-5-5); do not translate

On: when Whisper writes a 30-second decoding window as one long run without punctuation or all in capital letters, LectureFlow transcribes that window again with the preceding text as a prompt and keeps the new version only if it passes checks. “退化” = degenerate: the window's text lost its normal punctuation and capitalisation. Short; no period.

settings.asr.redecode_hint.notes: Hint of the row settings.asr.redecode. Keep all points: (1) on by default; (2) what triggers it: a 30-second window without punctuation or in all capitals; (3) what it does: that window is transcribed again with the text before it, and the new result replaces the old one only if it is better; (4) the cost: affected lectures take about 30–70% longer to transcribe, depending on the lecture (keep the numbers); (5) off: only the statistical repair runs (统计修复 = a text-only repair of capitalisation and sentence boundaries, no second transcription); (6) it applies to later transcriptions and does not make existing lectures need a rerun. Complete sentences.

settings.colab.memory_label.notes: Settings page, section “Colab remote transcription”, group “How to use” (settings.colab.use_title): the switch of Colab's memory mode, on by default (user's decision of 2026-10-27). On: the recording, the faster-whisper model and the Python packages stay on a RAM disk of the Colab runtime instead of its persistent disk; a lecture that does not fit uses the disk. Short; no period. Terms: 运行时 = runtime (the Colab machine, glossary §9); “Python 软件包” = Python packages, as in settings.comp.sources_hint.

settings.colab.memory_hint.notes: Hint under the switch settings.colab.memory_label. Keep all four points: (1) it is on by default; (2) the recording, the model and the Python packages stay in the runtime's memory and are not left on its disk; (3) when there is not enough memory, that lecture automatically uses the disk; (4) the boundary from SPEC-ext: the runtime is still Google's machine, so this does not make the data invisible to Google — never promise that Google cannot see it. Complete sentence(s). Terms: 运行时 = runtime (the Colab machine, glossary §9); “Python 软件包” = Python packages, as in settings.comp.sources_hint.

settings.colab.fast_label.notes: Settings page, section “Colab remote transcription”: the switch of “fast mode” (user decision 2026-10-27: an option, off by default). On the larger GPUs (L4, A100, G4) each lecture is cut at silent moments into parts that are transcribed at the same time. Short; no period. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture.

settings.colab.fast_hint.notes: Hint under the switch settings.colab.fast_label. Keep every point: off by default; only the L4, A100 and G4 GPUs (no effect on a T4); a lecture is cut at silences into 2–4 parts transcribed at once; 15–60% less time (about 1 minute for a 55-minute lecture on a G4); the result differs slightly from transcribing the whole lecture — about 3–4% of the words, and more differences in capitals, punctuation and where sentences break (be honest: never say it is the same); while on, these GPUs transcribe one lecture at a time instead of two at once. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Complete sentences.

settings.downloads.title.notes: Settings: title of the section (and its entry in the section list) for fetching the recordings the browser extension sends. Recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载): see glossary §9.

settings.downloads.intro.notes: Settings → Fetching: the line under the title. aria2c is the fetch tool's name: keep it.

settings.downloads.concurrency_label.notes: Settings → Fetching: how many lectures are fetched at the same time (1–6, a row of numbers). Wording: 同时刮削数 (user decision 2026-10-27: recordings are fetched, not downloaded; the spec said 同时下载数).

settings.downloads.connections_label.notes: Settings → Fetching: how many connections one file uses while fetching (1–16, a drop-down). Wording: 单任务连接数 (2026-10-27; the spec said 单任务线程数, but the value is a number of connections).

settings.downloads.connections_cap.notes: Settings → Fetching: grey text next to the connections drop-down: the platform's profile may set a lower limit (maxConnectionsPerFile), and the smaller one is used. Wording given by the lead.

settings.downloads.load_error.notes: Settings → Fetching: the section could not be loaded (with a retry button). Same pattern as settings.app.load_error.

settings.update.label.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, the user downloads the installer, and it is installed at the next start. Settings > App: title of the row with the update status, after “Update channel”.

settings.update.hint.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the small hint under the row title. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.privacy.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: privacy note with a shield icon under the status. “Mirrors” is the row settings.update.sources_label. Complete sentence with a period.

settings.update.state.idle.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: status line before any check since the start (a “Check now” button follows). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.checking.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: status line while a check runs (spinner). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.up_to_date.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last check found nothing newer. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.available.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: a newer version was found; a “Download” button and a line with the release date, installer size and “Release notes” follow. A “Beta” tag may follow for a beta release. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.downloading.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: download in progress, with a progress bar and “Cancel download”. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.importing.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: shown while the files of “Update from file” are checked (signature, version, size, SHA-256). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.pending.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the new version is downloaded (or imported from files) and verified; the desktop app installs it the next time it starts. A “Discard” button follows. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.check_failed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last check failed; the reason (errors.selfupdate.*) follows on the next line. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.download_failed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last download failed; “Download again” follows and the reason (errors.selfupdate.*) is on the next line. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.no_manifest.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the status line instead of “Checking for updates failed” (settings.update.state.check_failed) when the latest release has no update.json or signature yet (errors.selfupdate.no_manifest follows on the next line). settings.update.not_configured.unsupport.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the operating system or processor has no release package (3.x: Windows x64 and Apple silicon Macs only). Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.not_configured.no_source.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the updater could not start (no place for its files and settings; should not happen in a normal installation). Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.version_unbound.notes: In-app update: replaces errors.selfupdate.version_mismatch when the signature's trusted comment names no version at all (signed with minisign's default comment instead of LectureFlow's “lectureflow update version:…”). settings.remote.privacy.notes: Settings → Remote servers (ssh-1b): the user's own SSH inference servers (a Linux computer with an NVIDIA GPU, or an Apple silicon Mac) that transcribe lectures for this computer; experimental, shown only when switched on. The privacy note. “改用……处理” / “Process on …” refers to the lecture menu item menu.lecture.use_remote. Round 8 (C175b): the transcription prompt goes with the audio (the job.json without paths keeps initial_prompt; internal/stages asr_remote.go remoteParams, internal/remote params.go); files kept after a lost connection are removed only when the server's agent runs again after the retention time (internal/agent agent.go, jobs.go reap). Round 9 (TX-03, needs-human 一·11a): so the files expire about 2 hours after the connection ends (remote.DefaultRetain), and expired files are deleted the next time LectureFlow connects to the server; without another connection they stay there. Not “kept for at most 2 hours”, which is not true when LectureFlow never connects again. R89 medium 1: the files are kept so that the transcription can continue if the connection comes back soon, but a lecture waits only about 10 minutes for a lost connection (sshremote ReconnectGrace) before it goes back to this computer, so do not tie continuing the transcription to the 2 hours. “到期” (expire), not “过期”, which the glossary keeps for out-of-date stages. R85 low 1: deleted at once only after the result is back, a cancel, or an error of the run on the server (or a result that cannot be fetched or checked); an unfinished upload, a run the server refuses or a local write failure leave the files until the connection ends, then the retention applies (internal/sshremote transcribe.go).

system.devices.vram_low_missing.notes: Diagnostics page, transcription devices card: a warning under the device table about the NVIDIA card (cuda:0), shown instead of system.devices.vram_low when the device's model is also not installed (r6, T043). Typical case: a card with less than 6 GB, for which the setup guide installed large-v3-turbo or medium, while the device still names large-v3 from earlier settings; lectures then wait with waiting.model_missing and the user cannot tell why. Order: the cause first (the model is not installed, so the card cannot transcribe with it now), then why (the card's video memory is short of what the setup guide suggests for that model, so the guide recommends {suggest} for such a card), then what to do: switch the card to the installed {suggest} in the “Transcription” section of Settings (must match settings.block.asr); or, to keep {model}, install it under Components in Settings (settings.comp.title) — it may still not run or be slow. Advice only, nothing is changed; do not promise that switching makes transcription start, and keep “the setup guide suggests” (a suggestion, not a hard limit). Complete sentences with periods; system.devices.vram_queue_switch or vram_queue_estimate may follow (never vram_queue, the sentence about lowering the reserve: the wait is for the model).

system.devices.vram_queue.notes: Diagnostics page: sentence appended to an NVIDIA card hint (system.devices.vram_low, vram_model_missing or vram_queue_only) when the per-task estimate fits the VRAM available now but estimate + reserve do not (r2 T-PERF-02 / R37: judged by the free memory, as the scheduler admits a task). Say “likely”: the scheduler may still start a task in rare cases. “Each task needs” must match system.gpu.per_job, “Reserved GPU memory” must match settings.asr.vram_reserve. Only transcription on this NVIDIA card waits (other turned-on devices may take the task).

system.devices.vram_queue_estimate.notes: Diagnostics page: sentence appended to an NVIDIA card hint when the per-task estimate alone is more than the VRAM available now (avail_mb) and even the model recommended for the card (with its precision) does not fit once the reserve is added. The advice is to close other programs using GPU memory, or to turn on a CPU device or another transcription device in Settings. Say “likely”. “Each task needs” must match system.gpu.per_job, “Reserved GPU memory” must match settings.asr.vram_reserve. Only transcription on this NVIDIA card waits. “Transcription” must match settings.block.asr, “CPU” devices.kind.cpu, “Remote GPU (Colab)” devices.kind.remote; “turn on” as the device switch (devices.enable / devices.disabled). Since r2 T-PERF-02 the estimate follows the model and precision: no longer say the estimate cannot be changed in Settings.

Say “likely” for the waiting. The suggestion is advice; nothing is changed. “Each task needs” must match system.gpu.per_job, “Reserved GPU memory” settings.asr.vram_reserve, “Transcription” settings.block.asr, “precision” devices.precision.

system.ext.register_blocked.notes: Diagnostics page (ext web3), row "Browser extension connection", line under the "Register again" button after a registration, macOS only: the system refused LectureFlow access to the named browsers' registration folders. Tells the user what to do: allow LectureFlow under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access (use the names macOS shows in your language, as in errors.check.hint_browser_ext_full_disk), then click “Register again” (must match system.ext.register). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names.

system.ext.register_not_ready.notes: Diagnostics page (ext web3), row "Browser extension connection", line under the "Register again" button after a registration, macOS only: the named browsers are installed but have never been started, so they could not be registered. Open them once, then click “Register again” (must match system.ext.register). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names; “it” may need to become “them”.

system.ext.dev_extension_build.notes: Diagnostics page, row "Browser extension connection" (check browser_ext), a line under the browsers' registration. LectureFlow normally lets only the extension from the Chrome Web Store / Firefox Add-ons connect. This line says that this copy of LectureFlow also lets the developer build of the extension connect (the one loaded from the source code, “Load unpacked”), because LectureFlow itself is a development build (built from source, without a release version). Use the same name for the “developer build” of the extension as docs/install.md and the extension pages do.

system.ext.dev_extension_env.notes: Diagnostics page, row "Browser extension connection" (check browser_ext), a line under the browsers' registration. Like system.ext.dev_extension_build, but the reason is that the user (a contributor) set the environment variable LECTUREFLOW_DEV_EXTENSION=1 for an installed LectureFlow. Keep “LECTUREFLOW_DEV_EXTENSION=1” exactly as it is.

system.data_dir_restrict.notes: Button in the data folder row of the diagnostics page (#/system), shown with the warning errors.check.data_dir_shared / data_dir_readable: makes the data folder usable by the user's own account only. Same words as in errors.check.hint_data_dir_restrict.

system.data_dir_restricted.notes: Toast after “Restrict access” succeeded on the diagnostics page (#/system).

system.data_dir_rollback_reset.notes: Second toast after “Restrict access” on the diagnostics page (#/system): after the success toast, or after the error toast when restricting then failed (the removal had already happened); only when the data folder could be changed by other accounts before: the in-app update keeps what it needs to go back to the previous version after a failed update (its records and a saved copy of that version) in the data folder; other accounts could have changed them, so the program removed them. Nothing the user has to do: the next update makes a new copy. Not an error.

system.data_dir_restricting.notes: Label of the button system.data_dir_restrict (“Restrict access”) while the request runs, on the diagnostics page (#/system). Like system.ext.registering.

system.data_dir_restrict_title.notes: Title of the confirmation after “Restrict access” (system.data_dir_restrict) in the data folder row of the diagnostics page (#/system). The OK button is system.data_dir_restrict itself.

params.path: absolute path of the data folder

system.data_dir_restrict_confirm.notes: Body of that confirmation. Three things, none to be overstated: (1) the folder itself gets permissions for the user's account only, plus the operating system and the administrators (errors.check.hint_data_dir_restrict says so: do not promise “only you”), and its files and folders inherit them; nothing else on the computer changes. (2) In the parts that are run or trusted — the in-app update's files, the component environments, the app's own settings folder — items that belong to another account of the computer, or that carry permissions of their own that let another account change them, are made the user's and those separate permissions are removed. Do not say that other accounts can no longer read anything: only write access is looked at inside, and lecture folders are not gone through. (3) It only protects from now on: whether another account changed something before cannot be told from this.

menu.lecture.use_colab.notes: Lecture context menu action “Process on Colab instead” (改用 Colab 处理, SPEC-v3 V14.4): the transcription starts over on Google Colab. Terms: 借卡 = session, 使用时限 = usage window (not “fair use”), 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9). Short; no period.

menu.lecture.use_remote.notes: Lecture context menu (ssh-1b): sends the transcription to the SSH remote server {name} (a name the user gave it). With several servers it is a submenu whose title has {name} = “remote server”.

menu.course.export_cite_zh.notes: Course menu item, only in a Traditional display (P14.6): menu.course.export_cite with the Chinese converted.

menu.export.zh_hant.notes: Submenu at the end of a lecture's download menu (only in a Traditional display, P14.6): the text exports again, their Chinese converted. The hint beside it is menu.export.zh_variant_*.

menu.export.zh_variant_tw.notes: Small hint beside menu.export.zh_hant: the regional wording used.

menu.export.zh_variant_hk.notes: Small hint beside menu.export.zh_hant: the regional wording used.

menu.export.zh_failed.notes: Error toast: a converted (Traditional) download failed.

menu.export.vtt_en.notes: Download menu of the lecture page: English subtitles as a WebVTT file, made from the transcript when downloaded (available as soon as the transcript is done). Same pattern as menu.export.vtt_zh / vtt_bilingual.

menu.export.md_bilingual_desc.notes: Small second line under menu.export.md_bilingual in the download menus (T22 S4: a first-time user did not know what each format is): what the file is and what opens it, for someone who has never heard of Markdown. A .md file is plain text with formatting marks; do not name a particular program (it may not open it, or not be installed): say a Markdown editor or a notes app. Complete sentences with a period; it wraps in narrow windows, keep it short.

menu.export.vtt_bilingual_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.vtt_bilingual (see menu.export.md_bilingual_desc): a WebVTT subtitle file with both languages, loaded with the lecture's recording in a video player. Do not name a particular player.

menu.export.vtt_zh_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.vtt_zh (see menu.export.md_bilingual_desc): Chinese-only subtitles for the recording in a video player. Same shape as menu.export.vtt_bilingual_desc.

menu.export.vtt_en_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.vtt_en (see menu.export.md_bilingual_desc): English-only subtitles for the recording in a video player. Same shape as menu.export.vtt_bilingual_desc.

menu.export.cite_json_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.cite_json (see menu.export.md_bilingual_desc): the citation JSON is the transcript in a form another AI (a chat assistant the user gives it to) can quote: every sentence has a citation mark like [CSC1003 W02L1@12:34], so the AI's answers can say which lecture and moment a statement comes from. Not meant to be read by a person.

menu.export.txt_en_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.txt_en (see menu.export.md_bilingual_desc): the English transcript only, as a plain text file that any text editor opens.

menu.export.zh_hant_desc.notes: Second line under menu.export.zh_hant (only in a Traditional display, P14.6): its submenu downloads the same files with their Chinese converted to Traditional characters in the browser; the files the application keeps are not changed.

onboarding.step.storage.notes: Step rail label (3.1.0): the step that shows where the data folder is and lets the user move it (desktop app only).

onboarding.leave.notes: Quiet link at the top right: go to the workbench; setup continues from the same step next time.

onboarding.skip_tip.same.notes: Title (and accessible description) of the guide's “Skip” button on the steps that only explain (Welcome, Privacy): skipping does the same as the main button.

onboarding.skip_tip.computer.notes: Title of “Skip” on the step “Your computer”: what skipping leaves for later. Quote Settings section names exactly as settings.comp.title. Round 8 (R75 L7): choosing the local card on the next step (quote onboarding.asr_mode.local.name exactly) and continuing still picks the recommended components for the install (web/onboarding_mode.js proceed).

onboarding.skip_tip.asr_mode.notes: Title of “Skip” on the step “Transcription”. Quote the Settings section exactly as settings.block.asr.

onboarding.skip_tip.storage.notes: Title of “Skip” on the step “Data folder”: the same as its main button (quote onboarding.storage.keep exactly).

onboarding.skip_tip.providers.notes: Title of “Skip” on the step “Translation”. Quote the Settings section exactly as settings.block.providers.

onboarding.skip_tip.download.notes: Title of “Skip” on the step “Download” while a download runs: the same as its main button (quote onboarding.download.background exactly).

onboarding.privacy.title.notes: Title of the setup guide's privacy step (onboarding.js privacyStep). Round 9 (TX-03, needs-human 一·11a): not absolute. Lecture text goes to the model services, and with Google Colab or a remote server the recordings leave this computer (the step's own points say so), so the title does not say that all data stays here; it only says that the lecture files are kept on this computer.

onboarding.privacy.local.notes: Guide, step “privacy”: where transcription happens. Round 8 (C158b, AUD5 low 4): with Colab the transcription prompt (English terms of the glossary) goes along with the recording, as privacy.colab.1 says. Round 8 (C175b): the user's own SSH servers (settings.remote.*) get the recording and the same prompt too (internal/stages asr_remote.go sshRun: the job.json without paths, initial_prompt included; internal/sshremote transcribe.go uploads the audio), so both ways out are named.

privacy.intro.notes: The local privacy details page (#/privacy), linked from onboarding step 2.

privacy.local.2.notes: Privacy page, “What stays on this computer”. Round 8 (C175b): recordings leave this computer only for remote transcription. Google Colab has its own section below (privacy.colab.*); the user's own SSH servers have none, so this sentence says what they get and how long: the recording and the transcription prompt over SSH (internal/stages asr_remote.go, internal/sshremote transcribe.go); the job's files are deleted at once when the result is back, after a cancel or after an error of the run on the server; in other cases (an unfinished upload, a lost connection…) they expire about 2 hours after the connection ends (remote.DefaultRetain = MaxRetain, internal/remote/protocol.go; a per-server retain_min, not offered in the interface, can only shorten it) and are removed only when the server's agent next starts, i.e. the next time LectureFlow connects after that (internal/agent agent.go reap at every start, jobs.go keepJob / reap); if it never connects again they stay on the server. Same facts as settings.remote.privacy (R85 low 1). Round 9 (TX-03, needs-human 一·11a): hence not “kept for at most 2 hours”. “到期” (expire), not “过期”, which the glossary keeps for out-of-date stages.

privacy.sent.2.notes: Privacy page, what the model services receive: every item listed is sent (AUD5 low 4); keep the list complete. Original file names go with the title task and the file-name rule (at most 50, with upload and media creation times); the course name and code with the glossary cleanup and the file-name rule.

privacy.colab.1.notes: Privacy page, Google Colab: the recording and the transcription prompt (English glossary terms) are uploaded (AUD5 low 4). Round 8 (R85 medium 1): “only if” is about uploads to Colab, not about every upload: the user's own SSH servers get recordings too (privacy.local.2), so do not say recordings are uploaded only when Colab is on.

privacy.colab.2.where: list item on the privacy page, Colab section (account balance, available GPUs, runtime readings)

privacy.delete.1.notes: Privacy page, “Delete”. Only a lecture can be deleted (there is no deletion of a course, T22 S7). Round 9 (TX-03, needs-human 一·11a): the excerpts of model answers that a stage could not use (and the extra text after a JSON answer that was used) are written to logs/llm/rejected-<day>.jsonl in the data folder (internal/llm/calllog.go), by day, not by lecture, so deleting a lecture leaves them. Their files are removed when older than 14 days (CallLogKeepDays; earlier when the folder is over 128 MB), but only when LectureFlow next writes the call log on a later day, i.e. at its next request to a model service. So: they expire after about 14 days and are deleted at the next model request; never “kept for at most 14 days”. “到期” (expire), not “过期”, which the glossary keeps for out-of-date stages. R89 low 1: an answer of up to 16 KB is kept whole (RejectedExcerptBytes), only a longer one is cut to its beginning and end, so the text does not call them excerpts. R89 low 2: when log_level is set to debug (only in config.toml; Settings has no switch for it), the debug log writes whole requests and answers to logs/llm/<task>.jsonl (internal/llm/debuglog.go); they are not deleted with the lecture either and are pruned by the same rule (14 days, counted from the day a file was last written; at the next model request). Keep that sentence short and plain.

downloads.list_label.notes: Accessible name of the list of recording fetches above a course's lecture table (recordings the LectureFlow browser extension sent).

downloads.untitled.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Shown instead of the title when the recording platform gave none.

downloads.state.queued.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag (chip) of a fetch waiting for a free slot. Same word as the stage state 排队中 (glossary).

downloads.state.downloading.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a running fetch; followed by the progress (downloads.progress).

downloads.state.merging.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the fetched pieces (HLS segments, or the audio and the video track) are being joined into one media file.

downloads.state.importing.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the finished file is turned into a lecture draft (a few seconds), then transcription starts.

downloads.state.done.notes: State tag of a finished fetch (its lecture exists). The course page does not show finished fetches; kept for other views.

downloads.state.failed.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a failed fetch; the reason is on the row's second line, with a Retry button.

downloads.state.needs_refresh.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the recording site's sign-in (cookies) is no longer there or no longer accepted (e.g. after the app restarted, or it waited too long). The user resumes it by opening the recording page again and clicking the extension (downloads.needs_refresh.hint). Wording from the spec: 需要刷新.

downloads.state.cancelled.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a fetch the user cancelled (its files are deleted).

params.n: place in the fetch queue, 1 = next

downloads.position.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After the tag 排队中 / Queued: where the fetch is in the queue of all courses.

downloads.progress.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After the tag 刮削中 / Fetching (and 需要刷新: what is kept for resuming).

downloads.progress_unknown.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Progress while the size is not known yet (a playlist whose segments are still being counted).

downloads.track.audio.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). A track of the fetch that has no name from the platform's profile; tracks are listed after the title, e.g. “音频、视频”.

downloads.track.video.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). See downloads.track.audio.

downloads.needs_refresh.hint.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Second line of a fetch that needs a refresh (downloads.state.needs_refresh): what the user does to continue it; what was fetched is kept. Wording given by the spec (SPEC-ext, ext-brief §6.2). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No period. errors.downloads.restarted, credentials_rejected, credentials_expired, needs_refresh and credentials_cleared end with exactly this text (the page checks whether the reason already contains it): keep the six identical.

params.reason: why it needs a refresh, an errors.downloads.* sentence (e.g. the app restarted)

downloads.reason.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After downloads.needs_refresh.hint, in grey.

downloads.failed_unknown.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Second line of a failed fetch when the server sent no reason (normally an errors.downloads.* sentence is shown).

downloads.details.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Disclosure under a failed fetch's reason: opens the fetch tool's own message (aria2c or ffmpeg, in English). Same wording as the other “查看详情” the error texts point to (e.g. errors.downloads.merge_failed).

downloads.refused_hint.notes: 已废弃，不需要翻译或修改（DEPRECATED: no longer used by the download rows since r5, replaced by downloads.refused.*; do not translate or change). Earlier note: Course page, download rows: shown under the reason of a failed fetch when the lecture import refused the downloaded file itself (errors.upload.media_html / media_empty / media_playlist / media_format). Retrying imports the same file and fails again; sending it again from the browser extension downloads it anew.

downloads.refused.empty.notes: Course page, download rows: the reason of a failed fetch when the lecture import refused the fetched file itself (the task's error code is errors.upload.media_*; these replace the upload texts, which tell to upload another file). The row offers Remove only (no Retry: a retry would import the same file), so the text must not mention retrying; it says what was fetched and to send the recording again from the browser extension, which fetches it anew. Glossary: 刮削 = fetch (never “download” for recordings). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No final period, like errors.downloads.*. Case: the fetched file is empty (0 bytes).

downloads.refused.html.notes: Course page, download rows: the reason of a failed fetch when the lecture import refused the fetched file itself (the task's error code is errors.upload.media_*; these replace the upload texts, which tell to upload another file). The row offers Remove only (no Retry: a retry would import the same file), so the text must not mention retrying; it says what was fetched and to send the recording again from the browser extension, which fetches it anew. Glossary: 刮削 = fetch (never “download” for recordings). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No final period, like errors.downloads.*. Case: the fetched file is a web page, usually a sign-in or error page (the sign-in has probably expired).

params.kind: playlist type as detected, e.g. m3u8, mpd (not translated)

downloads.refused.playlist.notes: Course page, download rows: the reason of a failed fetch when the lecture import refused the fetched file itself (the task's error code is errors.upload.media_*; these replace the upload texts, which tell to upload another file). The row offers Remove only (no Retry: a retry would import the same file), so the text must not mention retrying; it says what was fetched and to send the recording again from the browser extension, which fetches it anew. Glossary: 刮削 = fetch (never “download” for recordings). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No final period, like errors.downloads.*. Case: the fetched file is a playlist or manifest pointing to other files; the extension's popup lets the user pick another track.

params.format: the detected container format name, e.g. tty, or ? (not translated)

downloads.refused.format.notes: Course page, download rows: the reason of a failed fetch when the lecture import refused the fetched file itself (the task's error code is errors.upload.media_*; these replace the upload texts, which tell to upload another file). The row offers Remove only (no Retry: a retry would import the same file), so the text must not mention retrying; it says what was fetched and to send the recording again from the browser extension, which fetches it anew. Glossary: 刮削 = fetch (never “download” for recordings). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No final period, like errors.downloads.*. Case: the fetched file's real format is not an allowed audio/video format; the extension's popup lets the user pick another track.

downloads.action.retry.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Button of a failed fetch: queue it again.

downloads.action.cancel.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Button of a fetch that has not ended: stop it and delete what was fetched. Also the confirm button of downloads.cancel_confirm.*

downloads.cancel_confirm.title.notes: Title of the question before cancelling a fetch that has already fetched something.

downloads.cancel_confirm.message.notes: Body of the question downloads.cancel_confirm.title. Buttons: downloads.action.cancel (danger) and downloads.cancel_confirm.keep.

downloads.cancel_confirm.keep.notes: The cancel button of the question downloads.cancel_confirm.title: closes it and the fetch goes on.

params.n: recordings queued, fetching, merging or creating their lecture (plural forms)

downloads.dash.active.notes: Workbench (dashboard): a line under the title while recordings sent by the browser extension are fetched, parts joined with “ · ”, e.g. “正在刮削 2 节录播 · 1 节需要刷新”, then links to the courses.

params.n: recordings whose fetch needs a refresh (plural forms)

downloads.dash.needs_refresh.notes: Workbench line (downloads.dash.active), in the warning colour: fetches waiting for the user to open the recording page again (downloads.state.needs_refresh).

downloads.dash.failed.notes: Workbench line (downloads.dash.active), in the error colour.

downloads.dash.course_unknown.notes: Workbench line: link text of a course whose name is not known (yet).

downloads.dash.open.notes: Workbench line: tooltip of the link to a course with fetches.

remote.state.offline.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.idle.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. Ready, but the connection was closed after a few minutes without work; it reconnects by itself.

remote.state.connecting.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. Also a lecture’s step on the server while LectureFlow connects.

remote.state.untrusted.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. The user has not confirmed the server’s host key yet.

remote.state.host_key_changed.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. The server presented another host key than the confirmed one; LectureFlow refuses to connect.

remote.state.auth_failed.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. The server refused LectureFlow’s key (its line is not in authorized_keys).

remote.state.unsupported.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.setup.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.installing.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.ready.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.busy.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period. Every slot of the server is in use.

remote.state.paused.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.

remote.state.error.notes: State of one SSH remote server, as a short chip in Settings → Remote servers, the resource panel and the diagnostics (ssh-1b). Short phrase, no period.
